fluff.overview: The Demon series of battle armor emerged from Gibson Federated BattleMechs during the Jihad as the companion line to the Word of Blake's Celestial OmniMechs. Conceived by Precentor Vapula, the Manei Domini's engineering chief, the six Demon designs draw their names from the malevolent figures of various world mythologies. Each suit was crafted to fill a specific combat role while projecting an element of psychological terror against the Word's enemies. Fielded almost exclusively by the cybernetically enhanced Manei Domini elite, the Demons share the same unsettling visual aesthetic as their larger Celestial counterparts and were rarely encountered outside the Shadow Divisions.
fluff.capabilities: The anti-infantry Se'irim replaces the standard model's anti-armor weapons with an arsenal designed for eliminating unprotected personnel. Two shoulder-mounted machine guns provide overlapping fields of suppressive fire, while a flamer in the right arm clears enclosed spaces and fortified positions. An anti-personnel weapon mount under the right forearm can carry a light secondary weapon. Battle claws on both arms replace the standard model's vibro-claw, enabling OmniMech transport and swarming attacks. The suit retains the base chassis's enhanced ground speed and stealth armor, making it an exceptionally lethal platform against conventional infantry. A single trooper in this configuration carries enough firepower to eliminate an entire platoon without assistance, and the anti-personnel mount seems almost redundant given the primary loadout's destructive potential.
fluff.deployment: Anti-infantry Se'irim troopers deployed in six-trooper Level I formations during Blakist pacification campaigns. The combination of stealth armor, enhanced ground speed, and overwhelming anti-personnel firepower made these formations grimly effective at suppressing resistance movements on occupied worlds. Each trooper carried enough weaponry to eliminate a conventional platoon single-handedly, and a full Level I could sweep entire city blocks with terrifying speed.
fluff.history:
The Se'irim entered service alongside the Asura in 3072 as its stealthy complement. Named for the satyr-like beings of Hebrew folklore, the Se'irim was the second of the two medium-weight battlesuits in the Demon series, but where the Asura was built mainly to be an up-front fighter, the Se'irim was styled for stealth. It eschewed jump jets entirely in favor of fast overland mobility and sensor-defeating armor designed to deter enemy ranged attacks. The tactical logic was clear: in the combined-arms formations Vapula envisioned, the Asura and the Celestials would draw the enemy's attention while the Se'irim positioned for devastating ambushes from concealment.

This doctrine of concurrent deployment was central to the Demon program. The Djinn and Asura had both entered service with a standard combat configuration and a stealth-capable anti-infantry version specifically intended to keep opponents guessing about which variant they faced. The Se'irim extended this principle to the formation level: any Blakist task force deploying Asura troopers might also have Se'irim teams lying in wait. Combined with the flexibility of the Celestial OmniMechs and the cybernetic enhancements of the Manei Domini operators, this layered approach created a range of capabilities that proved particularly difficult for conventional forces to counter.

The Se'irim saw action across several Jihad-era theaters. On Benjamin, a junior officer in the Forty-fifth Shadow Division developed what she called the "Choir" formation, roughly analogous to a Clan Nova: two Level IIs of battle armor organized with a BattleMech as a single combined-arms unit. During the Word's 3072 conquest of Benjamin, these Choirs deployed battle armor in advance of DCMS formations, then withdrew BattleMechs far enough to place the enemy in a killing zone between them. The tactic destroyed a company of Draconis Combine BattleMechs, vehicles, and captured several dozen warriors before Clan Nova Cat forces eliminated the formation's creator during a hot combat drop later that year.

On Arc-Royal, a specialized unit designated the "Demon Hounds," attached to the Forty-third Shadow Division, included at least one Level I of Se'irim during the Forty-third's ill-fated 3072 attack. Thought destroyed during the assault, the Hounds actually went to ground on Arc-Royal and spent the next two years conducting reconnaissance and espionage strikes aimed at weakening the planetary defenses from within. Their most daring operation destroyed a Kell Hounds munitions storage compound outside Old Connaught and caused significant damage to the Arc-Royal MechWorks facilities in New Hannover.

Initial speculation held that the Word's Celestial and Demon series were intended to eventually replace current equipment across all Blakist line forces. This never materialized. The Demon suits appeared in significant numbers only among the hyper-elite Manei Domini. Whether this was because the Demons were specially made to interface with Domini cybernetics at levels most modern battle armor could not match, or whether it reflected a deeper political rift between the Domini and the regular forces, remained uncertain.
